review.title: A Sandwiched Row and a Slow Squeeze
review.summary: The 12k as Black won, and Opus 5.5 resigned. The game was nearly level until move 8, when D5 lost 11.8 points and Black's lead jumped from +1.9 to +13.6. Opus 5.5 averaged 4.2 points lost per move against the 12k's 2.2, and it never got back into the game. Two more costly moves on the left side, B6 and B7, widened the gap to +25.9.

moments.text: The game turned here. Black led by only +1.9 before this move, and D5 lost 11.8 points, Opus 5.5's worst move, sending the lead to +13.6. The engine preferred E2. After D5, White's stones at C5 and D5 sit above a Black row on the fourth line.
The 12k's A3 lost 5.5 points, taking the lead from +17.7 to +12.2. The engine wanted E4. It was a real slip, but the lead stayed far above where it was before move 8.

The 12k's one blunder: D2 lost 8.6 points, and the lead dropped from +16.2 to +7.6. The engine's choice was E7. Black still held the advantage, and this was the nearest Opus 5.5 came to getting back into the game.
The chance did not last. C2 lost 6.4 points, and the lead went from +7.6 back up to +14.0. The engine preferred E6, and the 12k's blunder was undone in a single move.

Black's C6 had cost 5.7 points and the lead was +9.5, but B6 lost 8.0 points and sent it back to +17.6. The engine's choice was G5, on the open right side. Opus 5.5 kept pushing along the left edge instead.

B7 lost another 7.9 points, taking the lead from +17.9 to +25.9. The engine again preferred G5. By the final position the left-side White stones at B5, B6 and B7 are boxed in by Black at B8, C7 and C9, and the board shows no way back.

audit.reason: libs.py parses a pasted board and prints each group's stones and liberty count with a danger flag, and count.py flood-fills empty regions to tally territory with named dead stones removed. Both only inspect the current position and never try candidate moves or look ahead.
